newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Majority of Swedes against EU membership now - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Swedes against EU membership now - poll.

text.p: A large majority in all Sweden's political parties would vote against joining the European Union (EU) if a referendum were held now, according to a new poll published on Friday.

The poll by the Research Group for Social and Information Studies (FSI), published in political newspaper Dagens Politik, showed support for EU membership has fallen significantly since a 1994 referendum which secured Sweden's 1995 entry.
In the November 1994 referendum 52.5 percent of Swedes were in favour of joining the EU. Sweden joined in January 1995.
But the poll found that only 21 percent of members of the ruling Social Democrats party would vote in favour of joining the EU now compared to 45 percent in the 1994 referendum.
Support for EU membership among the conservative opposition party, the Moderates, has fallen to 52 percent from 87 percent.
Liberal party support has plummeted to 50 percent from 79 percent.
In the Centre Party 23 percent were pro-EU gainst 51 percent in 1994.
Among Christian Democrats only 25 percent would vote in favour of joining the EU, in the Left Party six percent and in the Green party 11 percent.
